Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of painful, itchy, cracked skin predominantly on the palms, worsening to impair work as a hotel housekeeper.
- Clinical impression: contact dermatitis likely related to cleaning product exposure; plan includes consistent glove use, topical corticosteroid, and frequent emollients with follow-up in 10–14 days.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Hand dermatitis: 3–4 months of severe dryness, cracking, soreness, and intermittent itch affecting mainly the palms; occasional bleeding only when scratched. Worsened recently; unable to work for the past 3 days.
- Pertinent positives: Itch (intermittent), pain, fissuring/cracking; mild generalized dryness on legs longstanding.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; appetite maintained.
- Occupational exposure: Hotel housekeeping; frequent use of cleaning agents (especially bathrooms); inconsistent glove use; job change ~4 months ago coincides with symptom onset.
- Prior treatments: OTC emollient (E45) without benefit; OTC antihistamine without benefit.
- Clinical impression: Contact dermatitis (likely irritant contact dermatitis from cleaning products).
- Plan (per consult): Avoid triggers; wear gloves at all times when cleaning; start topical corticosteroid cream; start stronger emollients applied liberally 3–4 times daily for 10–14 days; reassess if not improving in 10–14 days or sooner if worsening/spreading.

Issue 2:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- No complications discussed; no acute concerns raised in this consult.

Medications:
- Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- OTC E45 emollient — dose/route/frequency not documented (ineffective).
- OTC antihistamine — name/dose/route/frequency not documented (ineffective).
- Topical corticosteroid cream prescribed — name/potency/dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Stronger emollient prescribed — name not documented; instructed to apply 3–4 times daily.

Allergies:
- No known allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Social History:
- Occupation: Hotel housekeeper; exposure to cleaning agents; inconsistent glove use.
- Smoking: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: A couple of pints per week (minimal).
- Work impact: Off work for 3 days due to hand pain.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings: Not documented (telehealth; no in-person exam recorded).

Plan:
- Avoid cleaning product exposure; wear protective gloves consistently when cleaning.
- Begin prescribed topical corticosteroid cream as directed (details not documented).
- Apply prescribed/emollients liberally 3–4 times daily for 10–14 days.
- Return/telehealth review if no improvement within 10–14 days, or sooner if symptoms worsen or spread.
- Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy.

  - Specifics of prescribed topical corticosteroid (name, potency, dose, frequency) not documented.
  - Specific emollient product not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation (including metformin dose) not documented.
  - No vitals or physical examination findings.
  - No documentation of glycemic control or diabetic skin care counseling.
  - Vaccination and other preventive care history not addressed.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient initially reported “soreness in fingers” but later clarified symptoms mainly affect the palms (conflict noted).
